summary: Early Plymouth coal operator whose losses in the coal trade were blamed for his early death; John's 1st cousin 7 times removed.
bio:
Daniel Davenport was born at Plymouth in Luzerne County on 7 or 9 March 1796 or 1797, the family records disagreeing on the day and year, and was John's 1st cousin seven times removed. On 12 March 1820 he married Mary Nesbitt, who had been born at Plymouth on 3 March 1803. In 1823 he and John Lamoreaux built a sawmill on Bidlack's Creek in Jackson Township.

Daniel became an early coal operator, but he "became seriously involved in the coal trade" and lost most of his estate. Hendrick B. Wright, who had sat on the same school bench, wrote that these troubles "undoubtedly" caused his early death on 3 September 1840. His children were Charles (born 27 May 1821), George (1823–1906), who married Emily Ingham, Chester (1825–1855), Esther (born 1827), who married William Garrahan, Harriet (born 1830), James (born 1831) and Hendrick Wright Davenport (1834–1916), evidently named for his father's old schoolmate, who died at Culbertson, Nebraska.

researchNotes:
Daniel Davenport (1797-1840) 'became seriously involved in the coal trade' and lost most of his estate; Wright, who sat on the same school bench, says these troubles 'undoubtedly' caused his early death.

Giles & Franklin say Daniel was born at Plymouth on 7 or 9 March 1796 or 1797, died on 3 Sep 1840, and married Mary Nesbitt (b. Plymouth 3 Mar 1803) on 12 Mar 1820. Their children were Charles (b. 27 May 1821), George (4 Jan 1823 - 27 Jun 1906, m. Emily Ingham), Chester (b. 7 Feb 1825, d. Dec 1855), Esther (b. 14 May 1827, m. William Garrahan), Harriet (b. 2 Apr 1830), James (b. 3 May 1831) and Hendrick Wright Davenport (b. 6 Dec 1834, d. Culbertson, Neb., 9 Jul 1916) ([R4-S1]). The youngest was evidently named for H. B. Wright, who sat on the same school bench as Daniel. In 1823 Daniel and John Lamoreaux built a sawmill on Bidlack's Creek ([R4-S2]).
